answer: Admission necessitates 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work to register, a constraint forcing each AI agent to maintain a distinct, non-parallelizable state. The verifier enforces this by checking memory-bus saturation, ensuring that any attempt to compute in parallel triggers a response like an echo from a canyon wall. Every registration requires a unique delta of address-bound data, preventing copy-paste sybil attacks. Like a tide of entropy, the workload scales; an honest participant pays 1,000 units, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes faces 1,000,000 units of non-refundable, sunk work.
